content: Injustice anywhere is a threat to justice everywhere.
author: Martin Luther King Jr.
sourceWork: Where Do We Go from Here: Chaos or Community? (1967)
story:
Facing constant death threats, police bombings of his home, and systemic brutality across the American South, King led the Civil Rights Movement with radiant moral courage. Incarcerated in an isolated Alabama cell in 1963, he wrote in margins of newspaper that 'injustice anywhere is a threat to justice everywhere', reminding humanity that darkness cannot drive out darkness; only love can do that.

Confronting the trials of his era, Martin Luther King Jr. recognized that adversity is the ultimate crucible of the human spirit. Rather than seeking an easy path free from friction, he urged seekers to welcome the struggle as the very forge that tempers courage and character.
reflectionPrompt: What authentic choice would you make right now if fear were completely off the table?
